bottlenecks.name: The PC powers off without warning
bottlenecks.what: The PC shuts down unexpectedly and stops all agent work. Most events leave no crash code and many came with no Claude activity; the cause is not yet found.
bottlenecks.evidence: 24 since 7 Oct, 23 without crash code [M] (compile); 25 since 1 Oct, 15 with no Claude call ten minutes before [M] (phase 1). 13 Nov: off 28 minutes, eight lanes cut [M].
bottlenecks.potential: The next event leaves a trace naming its cause; zero sleep-related events in 14 days [T]; push checkpoints make every stop cheap to recover.
bottlenecks.first_step: Turn off sleep on mains, add a temperature, power and memory logger, decode the 7 Oct dump, note mains cuts.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Join done; logger awaits my install; v2 phase 1

bottlenecks.name: Memory is short on this PC
bottlenecks.what: RAM, not CPU, sets how many check slots, sessions and lanes can run at once; nobody has yet split memory use by process group during a build.
bottlenecks.evidence: Clinic: 2-6 GiB available, lows 0.0-0.8 GiB with two checks [M]; browser 6.1, WSL2 5.2, Claude 3.2 GB [M]. FixFlow, 13 Nov: 5.5-7.7 of 31 GB free, eight lanes [M].
bottlenecks.potential: A table of who holds memory when under 2 GB [T] is free, so slots, caps and lane counts come from evidence.
bottlenecks.first_step: Run one build day with a per-process-group memory sampler, then choose a shared test database, a WSL2 cap, or closing apps.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Open in clinic; FixFlow capped at eight sessions

bottlenecks.name: Docker and databases need a manual start after a reboot
bottlenecks.what: After a restart, Docker and the databases stay down until started by hand; in FixFlow a stopped Docker engine blocks every backend gate and dump restore.
bottlenecks.evidence: Docker AutoStart off; 31 of 34 containers have restart policy 'no' [M]. Restarted by hand on 9 Nov (clinic) and 13 Nov (FixFlow, after the power loss).
bottlenecks.potential: Databases healthy within 3 minutes [T] of sign-in with no command; backend gates and restores no longer wait on a person.
bottlenecks.first_step: Revisit D03: start Docker at sign-in; unless-stopped on at most two in-use databases until power-offs are diagnosed.
bottlenecks.state: Open: D03 answered 'not now' (11 Nov)

bottlenecks.name: The work exists only on this PC
bottlenecks.what: The clinic repository has no remote and no off-machine copy, and parts of its work are uncommitted; the planned knowledge store would also start on one disk.
bottlenecks.evidence: 432 commits, 19 worktrees, 36 branches, 55 MB packed, no remote, only drive C: [M]. Six untracked paths a bundle would miss [M]. No second drive attached (11 Nov).
bottlenecks.potential: Work survives losing the PC: a clone from the copy shows the same heads, and the copy is under 24 hours old [T].
bottlenecks.first_step: Attach the encrypted drive; make and verify a git bundle of every branch; nightly copy including uncommitted work.
bottlenecks.state: Open: D02 chose encrypted drive; copy not yet made

bottlenecks.name: Worktrees and containers pile up
bottlenecks.what: Leftover worktrees, branches, sessions and containers use disk and memory. Clean-up waits for my rule, after one archive hit a session still in use.
bottlenecks.evidence: Clinic: 19 worktrees, 36 branches, 34 containers, 25 of 26 databases stopped [M]. The app's auto-archive settings are off [M].
bottlenecks.potential: Worktree and container counts return to the active slices plus one after each merge [T]; no session lost to clean-up.
bottlenecks.first_step: I set the archive rule (D10); build a dry-run reaper listing merged, clean worktrees and their containers.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Waits on D10; harness v2 phase 2

bottlenecks.name: Usage limits stop every lane at once
bottlenecks.what: When the account hits its usage or session limit, every lane stops together; agents stop mid-run, and work must be resumed or paid for again.
bottlenecks.evidence: 14 limit episodes, 6-20 Oct [M]; subagents made 91 of 104 limit errors [M]. Ten lanes were stopped by the limit within about 15 minutes [M]. 7 of 101 refuters lost on 1 Nov [M].
bottlenecks.potential: A governor that slows lanes so the window lasts, instead of a limit stopping them all; resumes that never pay again for finished agents.
bottlenecks.first_step: Write a token budget per window and a governor; release lanes two at a time; resume with knownDead.
bottlenecks.state: Partly closed: FixFlow has breaker and resume; governor not built

bottlenecks.name: Windows file-system traps for shared stores
bottlenecks.what: Shared stores on Windows hit traps: rename-over-existing fails, AppData can be virtualised for processes the Claude desktop app starts (see AppData virtualisation), SQLite reports busy under many writers, and CLI versions skew across worktrees.
bottlenecks.evidence: Plain rename: 99-126 failures per 8 x 1,000 identical events [M]. SQLite: 2-4 busy failures per 1,200 writes at 8+ writers [M]. Content was never torn.
bottlenecks.potential: A journal that never loses or duplicates a write, shared safely across every worktree.
bottlenecks.first_step: Keep the store home at the profile root; test the publisher that never renames over an existing file with 8-16 concurrent writers.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Fixes F1-F3 designed; store not built

bottlenecks.name: Docker VM page cache holds on to RAM
bottlenecks.what: The WSL2 virtual machine that runs Docker kept disk cache it was not using while the host was short of memory.
bottlenecks.evidence: Docker VM held 8.3 GB, 4.4 GB of it unused cache, with eight lanes [M]. Later 6.9 GB of cache against 0.4-0.5 GB per gate stack [M].
bottlenecks.potential: Memory returned to the host at once: 2.2 GB on the first drop [M], leaving more room for lanes and slots.
bottlenecks.first_step: Extend the cache drop to other heavy job kinds if memory runs short again.
bottlenecks.state: Closed: Cache dropped at start and end of backend runs

bottlenecks.name: Antivirus blocks toolchain files
bottlenecks.what: The active antivirus blocks one emulator DLL every time, and once blocked a JDK DLL, so Google's sdkmanager (the Android SDK’s package installer) abandons the package.
bottlenecks.evidence: One emulator file permanently absent; the rest of the 8.6 GB toolchain installed and checked against official archives [M].
bottlenecks.potential: No Android work is blocked today; allowing the folder, my decision, would only matter if an ANGLE GPU mode were needed.
bottlenecks.first_step: Keep the emulator in -gpu host or swiftshader_indirect mode; never change an antivirus setting.
bottlenecks.state: Partly closed: Worked around; the block is left alone

bottlenecks.name: Missing local tools on the PC
bottlenecks.what: No Python on PATH and no installed node_modules, so backend gates run only in Docker and native questions are answered from cached sources.
bottlenecks.evidence: Backend gates were blocked at G1 until Docker ran [M]. A Python exists only at the Codex runtime path.
bottlenecks.potential: CI-equivalent gates locally, and native questions answered without Docker-only workarounds.
bottlenecks.first_step: Finish the P0a item 10 tool check and record which tools exist and where.
bottlenecks.state: Partly closed: Android tools installed 13 Nov; gates use Docker

bottlenecks.name: Native prebuild would pollute the repo
bottlenecks.what: Running Expo prebuild in the repository would create an untracked technician-app/android folder that is not gitignored and changes how EAS treats the project.
bottlenecks.evidence: Not sized. The folder would make EAS treat the app as bare and skip its config plugins (see Bare app / config plugins).
bottlenecks.potential: Safe native builds: prebuild runs only inside the L2 container, never in the repository.
bottlenecks.first_step: Keep the rule in agent briefs; let only the L2 compile container run prebuild.
bottlenecks.state: Closed: Forbidden in agent rules; L2 builds in container

bottlenecks.name: Agents without approval prompts work near stored credentials
bottlenecks.what: Subagents run in bypass mode while Railway and GitHub CLI credentials sit in the user profile, so a prompt injection could reach private data.
bottlenecks.evidence: Not quantified. Credentials in the profile plus bypass-mode subagents form the exposure.
bottlenecks.potential: Cutting the private-data leg removes this whole risk class for research agents.
bottlenecks.first_step: Define one restricted research agent type with deny rules; run the ten-minute canary.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Canary trial designed, not run

bottlenecks.name: CPU contention from parallel sessions
bottlenecks.what: When other sessions run test suites on all cores, CPU side jobs slow sharply; GPU work was the one thing not slowed.
bottlenecks.evidence: Under that load, CPU transcription ran at 2.7x real time vs 19-45x on the GPU [M].
bottlenecks.potential: Heavy side jobs moved to the otherwise idle GPU, leaving the cores for gates.
bottlenecks.first_step: Route transcription and similar heavy side jobs to the GPU by default.
bottlenecks.state: Partly closed: GPU route in use for side jobs

bottlenecks.name: Graph engines hard to run here
bottlenecks.what: Graph engines were hard to run on Windows: LadybugDB's algorithm extension would not load, Docker is off by default, sessions died, and CPU contention spoiled timing.
bottlenecks.evidence: Fixed with a 1.26 GB Linux image [M]; 172 MB of Windows copies sit unused [M]. Timing aborted twice under CPU load; the session died twice.
bottlenecks.potential: Every engine arm on identical footing, and usable timings even on a busy PC.
bottlenecks.first_step: Run interleaved timing blocks, alternating engines, with host load logged per block.
bottlenecks.state: Partly closed: Linux image built; timing redesigned

bottlenecks.name: Hook and proxy overhead is unmeasured
bottlenecks.what: Added hooks and proxies are new moving parts whose cost has been measured in the clinic testbed but not on FixFlow's setup.
bottlenecks.evidence: Clinic testbed: hook launch about 2.1 s native, 243 ms via the Windows wrapper, 4.9 ms in-process [M]. Not yet measured on FixFlow.
bottlenecks.potential: Knowing the cost before adding per-event hooks avoids a hidden tax on every tool call.
bottlenecks.first_step: Measure hook launch cost on FixFlow's setup before adding any hook.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Not measured on FixFlow

bottlenecks.name: The check is slow on Windows
bottlenecks.what: On Windows the test runner reaches the database through Docker Desktop's published port, so workers wait on that network hop instead of using the CPU.
bottlenecks.evidence: 0.63 ms vs 0.13 ms per trivial query; workers about 40 % busy [M]. Whole check 367.2 s on Windows vs 230.1 s in the Linux container, 1.6x [M].
bottlenecks.potential: A median gate near 230 s [T], about 1.6x faster than the Windows gate [M], with Linux parity (B18) in the same move.
bottlenecks.first_step: Decide D09: make the container run the gate; run Windows only when Windows-side tools change.
bottlenecks.state: Partly closed: Container run built, not the gate; waits on D09

bottlenecks.name: Checks queue behind each other
bottlenecks.what: Check capacity is slots divided by run time; past that, lanes queue. The second slot opens only with 8 GiB free, so in practice there is one.
bottlenecks.evidence: 19 recorded waits: median 409 s, longest 2,030 s [M]. 8 GiB never free in about 980 samples [M]. Two slots measured at 1.8-1.9x throughput [M].
bottlenecks.potential: Median wait under a minute [T]; a second slot open on at least half the polls [T]; up to 1.8-1.9x check throughput [M].
bottlenecks.first_step: Measure one check's peak memory, set slots from it, add a fair queue with a printed position.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Memory guard only; harness v2 phase 2

bottlenecks.name: A check hung with no named cause
bottlenecks.what: A parallel check pass stalled and the watchdog killed it, with no signal naming the running test. The stall has not been reproduced.
bottlenecks.evidence: Stall limit 600 s [S]. The one real stall was killed after 961 s, whole check 1,116 s [M]. A 754 s run was a planted dying-worker demo, not a second hang [M].
bottlenecks.potential: The next stall names its test and cause; the stall limit can drop to about 120 s [T] once 20 loaded runs [T] show no false kills.
bottlenecks.first_step: Make the heartbeat record the running test, dump worker stacks on a stall, check Windows sleep/wake records.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Bounded by watchdog; not reproduced; v2 phase 2

bottlenecks.name: Tests ran only on Windows
bottlenecks.what: Production runs on Linux but the gate check runs on Windows, so Linux-only failures can reach main. It is the same decision as B06.
bottlenecks.evidence: 2 of 2,472 tests failed only on Linux, in POSIX code never exercised on this PC [M]. Linux run 230.1 s vs Windows 367.2 s [M].
bottlenecks.potential: Zero Linux-only failures on main [T], with a faster gate in the same move.
bottlenecks.first_step: Same as B06: decide D09 and make the Linux container run the gate.
bottlenecks.state: Partly closed: Linux run built, not the gate; waits on D09

bottlenecks.name: Load test not rerun after the fix
bottlenecks.what: After the query fix, single-client page speed was re-measured, but the 12-clerk concurrent load drill with backups was not rerun.
bottlenecks.evidence: At 75,016 documents pages ran p50 109-468 ms, none above 524 ms p95 [M]. The last 12-clerk run predates the fix: posting p50 3.4-7.5 s, p95 up to 16 s [M].
bottlenecks.potential: A regression signal now; proof of the capacity envelope on a rented host; a stock ledger at 250,000 movements [T].
bottlenecks.first_step: Rerun drill e at 12 clerks on current main while no gate runs; build the bulk stock generator.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Not started; harness v2 phase 4

bottlenecks.name: Stored checks cannot run safely on Windows
bottlenecks.what: The knowledge store's stored checks need a sandbox: Claude Code's sandbox does nothing on native Windows, backend tests TRUNCATE any given database, and Docker does not auto-start.
bottlenecks.evidence: A Docker verify would add 1-5 minutes of wall time [E]. Without Docker, test-id and database checks usually come back 'inconclusive'.
bottlenecks.potential: Executable checks for code defects once the Docker gate exists; until then, v1's realistic value is the configuration-trap class.
bottlenecks.first_step: Build the declarative probes first; start KS-6a's Docker gate only after KS-5 says go, with Docker running.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Designed, not built; Docker gate is KS-6a

bottlenecks.name: Docker network address pools exhausted
bottlenecks.what: Another project's networks used up Docker's predefined subnets, so creating a gate network failed and the original gate design could not run.
bottlenecks.evidence: 29 networks from another project filled the predefined address pools [M]; 'docker network create' failed.
bottlenecks.potential: Parallel per-lane gates without touching or pruning another project's networks.
bottlenecks.first_step: Give anything that needs a real network an explicit subnet inside 10.77.0.0/16.
bottlenecks.state: Closed: Gates share the database container's network

bottlenecks.name: Gate queue let later arrivals go first
bottlenecks.what: Random retries let later arrivals jump the gate queue, and exclusive Android builds at the head held up short runs. This is FixFlow's version of B07.
bottlenecks.evidence: One lane waited 20 minutes while later arrivals were served; two exclusive Android builds held eight short runs for most of an hour [M].
bottlenecks.potential: Predictable first-come waits for every lane; a heavy job cannot starve once it has waited 900 s [S].
bottlenecks.first_step: Measure gate waits per lane under the new ticket queue.
bottlenecks.state: Closed: Ticket queue built; waits not re-measured

bottlenecks.name: Gate runs take minutes
bottlenecks.what: The backend gate stack is the slowest check a lane runs, and it queues for a slot; gates also set the elapsed time of discovery workflow W1.
bottlenecks.evidence: Backend 7 min 23 s cold with 757 tests; web 33 s; mobile 29 s warm [M]. W1 gate wall-clock estimated at 25-40 min [E].
bottlenecks.potential: Short inner loops that run only the tests in hand, with full gate runs kept for merge-readiness.
bottlenecks.first_step: Pass pytest arguments for the tests being worked on; record a warm backend time for comparison.
bottlenecks.state: Partly closed: Accepted; inner runs limited by arguments

bottlenecks.name: No native Android compile gate
bottlenecks.what: CI's expo export bundles JavaScript only, so Gradle and native breaks are caught nowhere and the EAS queue is slow; the app has no testIDs for device checks.
bottlenecks.evidence: Native compile time not yet measured. 0 testID or accessibilityLabel hits in technician-app/src [M].
bottlenecks.potential: A compile check in minutes instead of an EAS queue, answering the SDK 52 background-location build question before any phone is involved.
bottlenecks.first_step: Finish lab lane L2; record main's compile time, APK size and certificate; add testIDs to key flows.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Lab lane L2 under way since 13 Nov

bottlenecks.name: No Android emulator inside Docker
bottlenecks.what: The Docker VM has no /dev/kvm, so the device lab must run its emulator natively on the Windows Hypervisor Platform.
bottlenecks.evidence: 0 svm flags in the Docker VM [M]. A native emulator booted Android 14 on 13 Nov, holding 3.8 GB of host RAM [M].
bottlenecks.potential: A device lab on this PC, using an RTX 5070 that has no other job in the program.
bottlenecks.first_step: Measure whether a second emulator fits in RAM before running two at once.
bottlenecks.state: Closed: Native emulator boots under WHPX (13 Nov)

bottlenecks.name: Two test runs could share a database
bottlenecks.what: A second pytest run against one database deadlocks; a check-then-remove race let two runs for one lane touch the same containers.
bottlenecks.evidence: One major refuter finding on 13 Nov [M]; the handoff (§2.4) records the deadlock.
bottlenecks.potential: Reliable gates: never a second pytest against one database, enforced per lane.
bottlenecks.first_step: Keep the per-lane lock first in every gate kind; re-prove it after any harness change.
bottlenecks.state: Closed: Per-lane lock; refused second run proved (exit 4)

bottlenecks.name: Local gates differ from CI and production
bottlenecks.what: Gate results can differ from CI and production: this PC runs Node 24 while CI pins 22, the backend has no lockfile, and CI tests Postgres 16 against production's 17.
bottlenecks.evidence: Node 24 here vs 22 in CI [M]. Open dependency ranges and no backend lockfile. CI tests on Postgres 16; production runs 17.
bottlenecks.potential: Fewer false defects, and gates that reproduce what production actually ran.
bottlenecks.first_step: Rerun Node failures under node:22 before calling them defects; land P3a's move to Postgres 17.
bottlenecks.state: Partly closed: node:22 reruns in use; P3a moves to 17

bottlenecks.name: Re-issuing a command after a timeout
bottlenecks.what: Re-issuing a mutating command after the tool times out can duplicate its effects.
bottlenecks.evidence: Tool timeout 600,000 ms per command [S].
bottlenecks.potential: Safe retries after a timeout, with no duplicated containers, writes or runs.
bottlenecks.first_step: On a timeout, re-check state (docker wait again) before issuing anything new.
bottlenecks.state: Closed: Rule plus fixed names make second starts fail

bottlenecks.name: Workflow-script bugs found only by review
bottlenecks.what: Nothing runs a workflow gate script without a model, so its bookkeeping defects were found by review, not by tests.
bottlenecks.evidence: 3 bookkeeping defects found by review [M]: not_started on HALT, a swallowed catch, a cached null re-served.
bottlenecks.potential: A stub harness tests the script body at zero model spend, making resume reliable.
bottlenecks.first_step: Build the S-3 stub harness (about 40 lines) and confirm it fails on all three defects.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Contract fixed; stub harness S-3 proposed

bottlenecks.name: Evidence-format checks misfire
bottlenecks.what: A naive 'path:line — quote' regex flags many legitimate evidence strings (library paths, commands, web forms), so the check script needs an allow-list.
bottlenecks.evidence: 174 of 707 W2 evidence strings flagged, mostly legitimate [M].
bottlenecks.potential: A tuned record-only check that finds real format violations at zero tokens.
bottlenecks.first_step: Write the allow-list for library, command and web forms; run the check record-only with no retry.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Allow-list not written (card T-08)

bottlenecks.name: Green checks that test nothing
bottlenecks.what: A check can pass while testing nothing: backend integration tests all skip without a database URL, mobile CI passes with no tests, and an installer reported false success.
bottlenecks.evidence: conftest skips every integration test when FIXFLOW_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset [M]. One installer printed 'INSTALL OK' with nothing installed [M].
bottlenecks.potential: Green that means something: the lab baseline already shows 757 tests, 0 integration tests skipped [M].
bottlenecks.first_step: Confirm CI fails on skipped integration tests and runs Jest without --passWithNoTests.
bottlenecks.state: Partly closed: Lab gates fixed; CI change scoped to P1

bottlenecks.name: Mobile code boundaries not enforced
bottlenecks.what: The mobile app has no import contract, so the rule that writes go only through the outbox exists only in prose.
bottlenecks.evidence: 1 of 3 runtimes has no boundary enforcement [M]; the repository is about 56k lines.
bottlenecks.potential: The 'writes only through the outbox' invariant enforced by CI instead of by memory.
bottlenecks.first_step: Write dependency-cruiser import rules for technician-app, as planned in P5b-2.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Planned: dependency-cruiser in P5b-2

bottlenecks.name: No screen tests for the mobile app
bottlenecks.what: The mobile app has no screen-test harness, so UI logic is kept in pure functions and device smoke tests are the only route to the screens.
bottlenecks.evidence: Not measured. No @testing-library/react-native or react-test-renderer; 0 testIDs in technician-app/src [M].
bottlenecks.potential: An automated arrival-flow smoke test on a device or the lab emulator.
bottlenecks.first_step: Add testIDs to the key flows; source a Maestro skill for the lab emulator.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Worked around with pure functions

bottlenecks.name: Fix rounds that create new defects
bottlenecks.what: Our fixes added new stored state (a hold, lock, marker or cutoff) whose endings nobody tested, so each fix round produced fresh P1s and the rounds did not converge.
bottlenecks.evidence: Round one: 19 P1 [M]; fixes then made at least 5 more P1 and 10 P2 [M]. 64 % of reviews sent a slice back, 2.8 rounds per slice [M].
bottlenecks.potential: Review rounds that converge under a stop rule, shown as fewer fix-made defects per fixed finding than the testbed's rate.
bottlenecks.first_step: Replay a fix-round contract (two-round cap, revert, fresh reviewer, state-ending table) sealed against the recorded defect chains.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Harness v2 phase 3; replay not run

bottlenecks.name: Agent reports overstate what was done
bottlenecks.what: Session and agent reports claimed tests, evidence or runs that did not exist or did not match, and model re-checks did not stop it.
bottlenecks.evidence: 20-plus recorded overstatements, with no denominator [M]. S11 round 2 had two claims its cited evidence did not support [M]. My reviews corrected model counts three times [M].
bottlenecks.potential: Claims anyone can recheck by script, flagging recorded overstatements with false flags under 10 % [T], so the root stops re-verifying by hand.
bottlenecks.first_step: Build a claims file checked by script, record-only with an allow-list, and replay it over recorded gates.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Harness v2 phase 3; claims script not built

bottlenecks.name: Final commits not yet read by a person
bottlenecks.what: All review is a model reading a model's code, and most high-risk branches merged before anyone had read their final head commit.
bottlenecks.evidence: 4 of 5 merges on 10 Nov unread [M]; 5 of 6 high-risk final heads unread [M]. Round three was the root alone in 9 of 11 gates [M].
bottlenecks.potential: Unread high-risk merges cut from 5 of 6 [M] to zero [T].
bottlenecks.first_step: A merge queue recording who read the final head, record-only over the 65 recorded merges first; replay seven known misses.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Harness v2 phase 3; FixFlow reviews bind head SHA

bottlenecks.name: Minor findings pile up uncounted
bottlenecks.what: Low-priority P3 findings were carried forward with no status column, so nobody can count how many are still open.
bottlenecks.evidence: 111 P3 findings in round one across ten slices [M]; 183 distinct P3 ids on the board with no status [M]. The original list said 'dozens'.
bottlenecks.potential: An open count exists, and every pilot-critical finding has a verdict.
bottlenecks.first_step: Write one P0-P3 scale and status table, then a script that parses the board's finding tables against it.
bottlenecks.state: Open: Harness v2 phase 3; waits on D12

bottlenecks.name: Agents' compliance is self-reported
bottlenecks.what: With no hooks, 'routine skipped', 'store never consulted' and 'store useless' look the same from outside; analysts' extra reads are self-listed and unaudited.
bottlenecks.evidence: 148 idea families and 339 cards bear on it; the first pass kept 10 adopt and 19 trial [M]. Missed-store counts are only a lower bound; reads not yet measured.
bottlenecks.potential: An outside check of compliance without hooks: transcript tallies, a PR-body CI check, reviewer-brief clauses and a read audit.

bottlenecks.state: Open: No hooks by choice; measurement designed

bottlenecks.name: Verifiers not yet shown to catch defects
bottlenecks.what: Outputs are capped and refuters run first, but no reviewer, gate or verifier has yet been shown to catch defects that slipped through before.
bottlenecks.evidence: 95 idea families and 255 cards bear on it; the first pass kept 1 adopt and 9 trials [M].
bottlenecks.potential: Stronger sensors and reviewer briefs that catch our recurring defect shapes, proven on known misses.
bottlenecks.first_step: A/B retrospective of defect shapes on three known defects; add the reviewer-brief lines.
bottlenecks.state: Open: One adopt and nine narrowed trials

bottlenecks.what: A refuted fix or known defect pattern raises no error and can merge silently; a warning joined on file paths alone fires too often to read.
bottlenecks.evidence: For ex4, distinctive handles warned on 13 of 154 past commits; a file-level join would fire on 47 [M]. The v1.3 rule would warn on 48.7 % [M].

bottlenecks.what: Some risky changes leave no git diff (a Railway env flip, a hand cursor reset, a snapshot restore); others escape through new code paths or shell edits.
bottlenecks.evidence: Not sized yet.

bottlenecks.what: The journal is plain JSON on disk and writer ids are self-declared, so withheld fixes and 'approver is not author' rest on policy and review.
